description: `plugin/governance/remediation-doctrine.md` `### Recorded Residual` is the single source for the SECOND sanctioned destination of an actionable finding left unfixed in a review loop: a decision recorded in the repository rather than work filed on a tracker. The source pin is ONE span carrying BOTH halves of that conditional rule: the discriminating condition (a residual is admissible ONLY on one of two grounds, the attacker or failure being outside the recorded threat model, or no fix on this engine being able to close the class by user decision, together with the sentence that origin is not a ground) and the obligation either ground triggers (leave the finding unfixed as a recorded residual and write the reasoning into the repository adjacent to the code it concerns). Deleting or rewriting either half, re-adding origin as a ground, or dropping one of the two grounds turns the suite red. A second pin in the same file carries the section's opening exclusion, that a found, fixable root cause, introduced or inherited, is never recorded in place of a fix; deleting it turns the suite red. The consumers pin the POINTER only, never remedy prose, so honest rewording of the doctrine body does not break them: `plugin/governance/decision-autonomy.md` and `plugin/agents/overlord.md` must still name `### Recorded Residual` in the doctrine file, `plugin/agents/cerebrate.md` must still name the section by its doctrine-term form alongside Defer-with-Scope, and `plugin/skills/decision-report/SKILL.md` must still carry the fire-condition enum that admits `recorded` beside `did-now` and `deferred`, the coupling that keeps the fourth disposition reportable. What this pin honestly guarantees is exactly that these word sequences exist in these five named files; it claims nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion that leaves the pinned bytes intact is invisible: surrounding prose that adds a third ground, that turns the two grounds into conjunctive conditions, or that re-routes the destination to a tracker entry stays green; (2) the sentence tail carrying the destination examples, the required contents of the record, and the `open NO tracker entry` clause is deliberately OUTSIDE the pinned span, so that the destination examples stay cheap to reword honestly, and deleting that tail alone stays green; (3) the pin sees only the five files it names: a further consumer that drops its pointer is invisible, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW consumer that never carries the pointer at all, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

source.pattern: A residual is admissible only on one of two grounds: - **Outside the threat model.** The attacker or failure the finding assumes is outside the recorded threat model, per **Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings**. - **Unclosable on this engine.** No fix on this engine can close the class, and the user decided so. Origin is not a ground. "Inherited" is a universal escape hatch that launders real work into a silent drop. On either ground, the finding is left unfixed as a recorded residual: write the reasoning into the repository adjacent to the code it concerns

consumers.pattern: A found, fixable root cause, introduced or inherited, is never recorded in place of a fix.
